conditions: Turn the Air must print an Adept-row value for its cold figure, whose row floor is five, or declare the chip on the card as a leveled condition with its level named; the printed value one must not remain.
Ward of Iron's Strong clause must print a Master-row value (seven, ten or fourteen) or a sanctioned tier step in place of the bare four; the value four must not remain on the card.
The locked rows 4/6/8, 5/8/11 and 7/10/14 and the cantrip line 1/3/5 must not be amended to accommodate either card; both corrections are made on the card.
The Ember Lance derived pair (three behind six, four behind eight) and the illustration's position after the final Wind card are closed findings and must not be reopened or re-filed under t-01.
No cantrip's exempt figure may be cited as licence for a sub-row figure printed on a tiered card.

The unrebutted chapter-local wording items stay inside t-01 as editorial repairs and do not create a new topic: strike the header modifier no rung of the same card uses at 11:438, 11:541 and 11:604, and re-name Paperweight's coin-keyed object and close its open-ended strongest rung at 11:133 and 11:137.
point_of_contention: Whether t-01's card-level refutes still describe chapter 11 as it now stands after the merge, and which off-row damage figures remain live defects, to be cleared by what repair.
reasoning: On the arguments as presented, t-01 has shrunk to two live items and the rest is spent. f-005's load-bearing arithmetic, a derived two set against a headline of six, is conceded by its own author in f-030, who reports the merged middle line now reads three, and is independently recomputed by f-038, whose census finds the merged text prints the exact halves three and four against six and eight; both agree the filing describes text the chapter no longer carries, so it loses. f-021's subject was position alone, and f-036 reports the merged file places the plate, its caption and its closing break after the last Wind card and immediately before the next section heading, which is the pattern f-021 itself measured at ten sibling sites; that refute loses as implemented. f-006 and f-010 do not survive whole: their reading-ambiguity half is withdrawn by f-031, which reports the Strong clause now names a single reflected consequence, but their second half is left standing on purpose, because the surviving four sits three under the Master floor of seven and equals the Novice row's first value, and f-038's independent census counts that figure among the off-row figures on the merged text. f-009 is attacked twice and survives both: f-033 shows the comparand is a cantrip whose figures come from an exempt one/three/five line and cannot license a sub-row figure on a tiered card, and f-038 shows the licensed homes for a sub-row figure, a leveled condition as at Brimstone Burst or the row itself as at 05:584, are not the shape this card writes; neither rebuttal restores the printed one, and both concede it sits four under the Adept floor of five. The only thing that changes is its class: the repair is a single numeral, so MECHANICAL rather than DESIGN. The framing and disposition filings f-027 and f-028 went unrebutted and are taken as the topic's working disposition, with the block-level census question and the card-versus-conventions wording items kept inside t-01 rather than made a fresh topic.
ruling: The council must close t-01's two refutes that describe pre-merge text - the Ember Lance follow-through and the misplaced illustration - and must treat Turn the Air's one point of cold on an Adept card and the bare four on Ward of Iron's Strong line as the only live off-row figures, repairing each by keying the figure to the row its own card owns or by declaring it a leveled condition; no locked row, band or cantrip line may be amended to absorb them, and the chapter-local wording items already recorded under t-01 stay editorial repairs inside this topic.

conditions: The three arcane Protection cards at 11:643, 11:650 and 11:657 must be renamed on the primal precedent at 12:170, 12:204 and 12:227 to tradition-distinct titles, or removed from chapter 11; no two traditions may ship identically titled Protection cards.
The ward ladder's figures must not change: ranks 1/1, 2/2 and 3/3 against grants of one, two and three, and a top value of three against the tier caps three, four and six, stay as printed.

The DR conflict between the owner's one-source rule and its duration carve-out must be filed against the DR-owning chapter's carve-out paragraph and its five named granters, not against chapter 11 or any ward card; each ward card's no-stacking line stays.

The header-tag filing is accepted only as its residue: the paired tags must print in one consistent order at 11:375/11:541 and 11:456/11:521, and the Ward tag must not be spent on cards that grant no damage reduction while the same section names its DR ladder Ward.
The plant heading at 11:334 keeps its plural; any repair to the divergent plant heading is made in the divine spell list.
The cantrip line and this chapter's three cantrip top rungs at 11:56, 11:101 and 11:110 do not move; the crossing with the Novice floor is repaired in the magic-system chapter's comparative clause.

The closed items must not be reopened under t-03: the permanent-until-dispelled duration and the ritual casting-time entries are fixed on the merged text, and the missing book-level definitions for ending an effect by magic and for the header mode word are carried as cross-chapter items, not re-filed against chapter 11.
point_of_contention: Whether t-03's five supporting filings outweigh its two refutes - whether the shared Protection card names and the header-tag vocabulary are defects chapter 11 must repair, or whether the owning chapters carry them and the topic closes.
reasoning: The five supporting filings carry the weight they were filed on, and three of them dispose of the refutes directly. f-008's split-model claim fails on independent recomputation: f-032, f-039 and f-040 all confirm the owner keeps one governing source and takes the higher, that its worked example resolves this ladder's middle card against light armour by the larger single number, and that the adding paragraph's five granters are four class capabilities and one talent at 05:581, 05:585, 05:681, 05:683 and 09:94 with no ward among them; f-032 also corrects its own round-one arithmetic to a one-point delta and concedes the tension belongs to the owning chapter, and f-039 adds that the adding bucket sums to eight, past the Master ceiling of six. f-015 and f-017 are closed on the page: f-034 reports no occurrence of the disputed duration word and f-035 reports all three action slots legal with the timing moved into the range bracket, so both describe pre-fix text, and their book-level residue, no definition for ending an effect by magic and no defined mode word for the header field, is carried rather than re-filed here. f-012's conformance case is confirmed by f-039 and f-040: ranks one, two and three against grants one, two and three with exact equality, a ladder maximum of three against caps three, four and six, and a card-level no-stacking line that governs the ward. f-016's inventory, f-020's eight agreeing cross-references and f-022's point that 11:334 carries the plural the Discipline owner prints all went unrebutted. f-025's cantrip-versus-Novice crossing is likewise unrebutted and correctly assigns the edit to the owning chapter's comparative clause rather than to this file's rungs. That leaves the two refutes. f-003's headline is destroyed by f-029: the census reproduces but the inference does not, because the sibling spell list keeps fifteen private tags and the Discipline chapter twenty-five against this chapter's ten, so a private vocabulary is what those chapters already do; only the narrow residue survives. f-001 is different in kind: no supporting filing ever engaged it, and f-037, filed by the other refuter, concedes f-008, f-015 and f-017 while stating that f-001 stands as filed; f-040 records the same naming risk and declines to file it. A charge that was never successfully attacked stands. So the five supporting filings outweigh the two refutes on every axis the refutes contested except the duplicated card names, which is the one live defect t-03 leaves in this chapter, with the remaining residues owed by the owning chapters.
ruling: The council must rule t-03 for the supporting filings on every axis they engaged - the ward ladder, the card inventory, the cross-chapter references, the plant heading and the cantrip comparison - and must require the one charge they never answered to be repaired: the arcane Protection trio must not ship under the divine chapter's titles, while the header-tag filing survives only as its narrow residue and every other surviving item is charged to the owning chapter rather than to chapter 11.
